core_evidence.title: MAPEX: Modality-Aware Pruning of Experts for Remote Sensing Foundation Models
core_evidence.authors: Joelle Hanna; Linus Scheibenreif; Damian Borth
core_evidence.abstract: Remote sensing data is commonly used for tasks such as flood mapping, wildfire detection, or land-use studies. For each task, scientists carefully choose appropriate modalities or leverage data from purpose-built instruments. Recent work on remote sensing foundation models pre-trains computer vision models on large amounts of remote sensing data. These large-scale models tend to focus on specific modalities, often optical RGB or multispectral data. For many important applications, this introduces a mismatch between the application modalities and the pre-training data. Moreover, the large size of foundation models makes them expensive and difficult to fine-tune on typically small datasets for each task. We address this mismatch with MAPEX, a remote sensing foundation model based on mixture-of-modality experts. MAPEX is pre-trained on multi-modal remote sensing data with a novel modality-conditioned token routing mechanism that elicits modality-specific experts. To apply the model on a specific task, we propose a modality aware pruning technique, which only retains experts specialized for the task modalities. This yields efficient modality-specific models while simplifying fine-tuning and deployment for the modalities of interest. We experimentally validate MAPEX on diverse remote sensing datasets and show strong performance compared to fully supervised training and state-of-the-art remote sensing foundation models. Code is available at https://github.com/HSG-AIML/MAPEX.
core_evidence.method: modality-conditioned token routing and expert pruning
core_evidence.contribution: shows modality-conditioned expert routing and pruning are existing EO FM operations
core_evidence.limitation_gap: routes modalities to pretrained experts rather than generating spatially local task decision operators from paired optical-SAR evidence

core_evidence.title: MaRS: A Multi-modality Very-high-resolution Remote Sensing Foundation Model with Cross-Granularity Meta-Modality Learning
core_evidence.authors: Ruoyu Yang; Yinhe Liu; Heng Yan; Yiheng Zhou; Yihan Fu; Han Luo; Yanfei Zhong
core_evidence.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
core_evidence.abstract: The multi-modality remote sensing foundation model (MM-RSFM) has made notable progress recently. However, most existing approaches remain limited to medium-resolution, single-modality, restricting their performance in fine-grained downstream applications such as disaster response and urban planning. In this work, MaRS is proposed, a multi-modality very-high-resolution (VHR) remote sensing foundation model designed for cross-modality granularity interpretation of complex scenes. To achieve this, a multi-modality VHR SAR-optical dataset, MaRS-16M, is constructed through large-scale collection and semi-automated processing, comprising over 16 million paired samples. Unlike previous work, MaRS tackles two fundamental challenges in VHR SAR-optical self-supervised learning (SSL) techniques. Cross-granularity contrastive learning (CGCL) is introduced to alleviate alignment inconsistencies caused by imaging differences, and meta-modality attention (MMA) is designed to unify heterogeneous physical characteristics across modalities. Compared to existing remote sensing foundation models (RSFMs) and general vision foundation models (VFMs), MaRS performs better as a pre-trained backbone across nine multi-modality VHR downstream tasks.
core_evidence.contribution: establishes cross-granularity multimodal foundation representation as prior art
core_evidence.limitation_gap: foundation-model pretraining and different resolution regime not a downstream fixed-CROMA conditional classifier

core_evidence.title: SkySense V2: A Unified Foundation Model for Multi-modal Remote Sensing
core_evidence.authors: Yingying Zhang; Lixiang Ru; Kang Wu; Lei Yu; Lei Liang; Yansheng Li; Jingdong Chen
core_evidence.abstract: The multi-modal remote sensing foundation model (MM-RSFM) has significantly advanced various Earth observation tasks, such as urban planning, environmental monitoring, and natural disaster management. However, most existing approaches generally require the training of separate backbone networks for each data modality, leading to redundancy and inefficient parameter utilization. Moreover, prevalent pre-training methods typically apply self-supervised learning (SSL) techniques from natural images without adequately accommodating the characteristics of remote sensing (RS) images, such as the complicated semantic distribution within a single RS image. In this work, we present SkySense V2, a unified MM-RSFM that employs a single transformer backbone to handle multiple modalities. This backbone is pre-trained with a novel SSL strategy tailored to the distinct traits of RS data. In particular, SkySense V2 incorporates an innovative adaptive patch merging module and learnable modality prompt tokens to address challenges related to varying resolutions and limited feature diversity across modalities. In additional, we incorporate the mixture of experts (MoE) module to further enhance the performance of the foundation model. SkySense V2 demonstrates impressive generalization abilities through an extensive evaluation involving 16 datasets over 7 tasks, outperforming SkySense by an average of 1.8 points.
core_evidence.method: shared transformer backbone with adaptive patch merging modality prompts and mixture of experts
core_evidence.dataset: sixteen Earth-observation datasets across seven tasks
core_evidence.contribution: establishes modality-aware prompts resolution handling and experts as MM-RSFM design axes
core_evidence.limitation_gap: pretraining-scale model rather than a 3090-bounded downstream optical-SAR segmentation operator
core_evidence.core_evidence_reason: direct multimodal EO foundation-model architecture boundary

prior_art_evidence.authors: Harel Yadid; Meir Yossef Levi; Roy Betser; Guy Gilboa
prior_art_evidence.abstract: SING decomposes a linear classifier head with SVD into principal and null subspaces, constructs feature perturbations that preserve logits, and interprets the semantic content of classifier invariants through a vision-language translator.

prior_art_evidence.method: SVD decomposition of the final linear head into principal and null projectors with logit-equivalent feature perturbations

prior_art_evidence.limitation_gap: does not constrain a paired optical-SAR residual, preserve its tangent component while bounding class-normal displacement, or evaluate dense EO segmentation

critic_conclusions.narrowest_defensible_delta: Unlike CLEAR, which estimates data-level visual–text covariance and suppresses its dominant shared singular directions, CTSP uses the existing shared segmentation head only as detached, sample-invariant geometry at a fixed final fusion interface, preserving the classifier-null part of an already-formed optical–SAR residual while capping its normalized class-logit-visible part; any benefit must be demonstrated by a ≥2.0 pp mIoU gain and a matched whole-residual scalar-shrink control.
critic_conclusions.what_is_not_new: SVD/pseudoinverse, classifier row/null geometry, orthogonal or tangent decomposition, residual clipping, trust regions, multimodal safety/redundancy suppression, optical-SAR fusion, CROMA, SEN12TS, CE+Lovasz, pretrained initialization, or the 24-epoch protocol.
critic_conclusions.mandatory_rebuttal: The claim fails if C2's matched whole-residual shrink is practically indistinguishable, if C1 is equal/better, if the projector is inactive/degenerate, or if a later exact same-operation prior is found.
critic_conclusions.source_status: Seven high-potential records were checked through official CVF PDFs, official arXiv HTML, or publisher HTML. The broader 102-record set remains abstract/metadata triage and does not prove absence.

integrity_rule: Canonical core records exactly match the frozen library; V19 targeted priors are separately source-grounded and do not assert absence or support.
